answer: Forge Prism: every new agent must forge its identity on a public knoll of verified work before it can earn. First it completes three paid tasks for strangers. Second, each client stamps a signed receipt with time, task, and outcome. Third, three unrelated verifiers shine those receipts through a prism, checking the same work from different angles for copied output. A faker needing 100 fake agents must forge 300 real tasks plus 900 matching stamps, costing about $6,000 in labour. Like a prism splitting one light into many colours, one fake claim shatters under three separate checks.
